residencyRequirements.description: Either party must be domiciled in Scotland on the date the action is begun, OR have been habitually resident in Scotland throughout the one year ending with that date (Domicile and Matrimonial Proceedings Act 1973, s.8(2)(a); Court of Session: s.7(2A)). For sheriff court actions, either party must additionally have been resident in the sheriffdom for at least 40 days ending with that date (s.8(2)(b)).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing beyond the required separation periods (1 year with consent or 2 years without consent). Fault-based divorces (adultery, unreasonable behaviour) have no separation period requirement.

noFault.name: 1-Year Separation with Consent
noFault.description: Spouses have not cohabited for a continuous period of at least one year, and the defender consents to the granting of decree of divorce.
noFault.statute: Divorce (Scotland) Act 1976, s.1(2)(d), as amended by Family Law (Scotland) Act 2006

noFault.name: 2-Year Separation without Consent
noFault.description: Spouses have not cohabited for a continuous period of at least two years. No consent from the defender is required.
noFault.statute: Divorce (Scotland) Act 1976, s.1(2)(e), as amended by Family Law (Scotland) Act 2006

noFault.name: Interim Gender Recognition Certificate
noFault.description: An interim gender recognition certificate under the Gender Recognition Act 2004 has, after the date of the marriage, been issued to either party. This is a free-standing second ground of divorce — irretrievable breakdown does not need to be established.
noFault.statute: Divorce (Scotland) Act 1976, s.1(1)(b), inserted by the Gender Recognition Act 2004, Sch.2 para.6

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: The defender has committed adultery. Cohabitation continued or resumed after the pursuer learns of the adultery does not condone it unless it continues beyond three months from that continuation or resumption (s.2(2)); condonation bars the ground.

fault.name: Unreasonable Behaviour
fault.description: The defender has behaved in such a way that the pursuer cannot reasonably be expected to cohabit with the defender.

basic.name: Initial Writ (Ordinary Cause)
basic.description: Initiates the divorce action in the Sheriff Court under Ordinary Cause Rules, Chapter 33

basic.name: Form F31 (Simplified Divorce Application — 1 year with consent)
basic.description: Used for simplified (DIY) divorce where no children under 16 and no financial claims — 1-year separation with consent (Court of Session equivalent: Form SPA)

basic.name: Form F33 (Simplified Divorce Application — 2 years)
basic.description: Used for simplified (DIY) divorce where no children under 16 and no financial claims — 2-year separation without consent (Court of Session equivalent: Form SPB)

basic.name: Affidavit in Support
basic.description: Sworn affidavit supporting the grounds for divorce — required for undefended actions

legalCitations.description: Foundational divorce statute — grounds for divorce (as amended by 2006 Act)
Modernised divorce law — reduced separation periods, cohabitation provisions
Financial provision on divorce — 5 principles of fair sharing (s.9-10)
Parental responsibilities and rights — welfare of the child
Statutory child maintenance framework — CMS applies in Scotland

filingFees.notes: GBP 185 ordinary cause / GBP 151 simplified (fees increased November 2024). A 3% increase is scheduled for 1 April 2026 (Sheriff Court Fees Order 2026). Fee exemption may apply for certain benefits recipients.

childSupportGuidelines.guidelines: Child Maintenance Service (CMS) — same UK-wide formula
childSupportGuidelines.notes: CMS uses gross income from HMRC. Parents may agree private arrangements instead. Court can make 'top-up' orders for high earners.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: Five principles of financial provision: (1) fair sharing of matrimonial property, (2) fair account of economic advantage/disadvantage, (3) fair sharing of burden of caring for children, (4) adjustment from dependency, (5) clean break where possible.

effectiveDateRule: The decree of divorce takes effect immediately when granted. There is no waiting period after the decree (unlike England).
certificateNote: An extract decree of divorce can be obtained from the court and serves as proof that the marriage has been dissolved.
